entities: germ cells and adult stem cells

triples.head: DNA polymerase
triples.evidence: The essential steps of replication are the same as in prokaryotes. Before replication can start, the DNA has to be made available as a template.

triples.head: Helicase
triples.evidence: A helicase using the energy from ATP hydrolysis opens up the DNA helix.

triples.head: Primase
triples.evidence: Primers are formed by the enzyme primase, and using the primer, DNA pol can start synthesis.

triples.head: DNA pol α
triples.evidence: DNA pol α adds a short (20 to 30 nucleotides) DNA fragment to the RNA primer on both strands, and then hands off to a second polymerase.

triples.head: DNA pol ε
triples.evidence: While the leading strand is continuously synthesized by the enzyme pol ε, the lagging strand is synthesized by pol δ.

triples.head: DNA pol δ
triples.evidence: While the leading strand is continuously synthesized by the enzyme pol ε, the lagging strand is synthesized by pol δ.

triples.head: PCNA
triples.evidence: A sliding clamp protein known as PCNA (proliferating cell nuclear antigen) holds the DNA pol in place so that it does not slide off the DNA.

triples.head: RNase H
triples.evidence: The displaced primer RNA is then removed by RNase H (AKA flap endonuclease) and replaced with DNA nucleotides.

triples.head: DNA ligase
triples.evidence: The gaps that remain are sealed by DNA ligase, which forms the phosphodiester bond.

triples.head: Telomerase
triples.evidence: The telomeres are added to the ends of chromosomes by a separate enzyme, telomerase.

triples.head: Telomerase
triples.evidence: The telomerase enzyme contains a catalytic part and a built-in RNA template.

triples.head: Telomerase
triples.tail: germ cells and adult stem cells
triples.evidence: Telomerase is typically active in germ cells and adult stem cells.
